comment: Keystone THREADS for the year, plus the recap ITEMS the built lessons have authored. Under DFM 134 the Do-Now serves a pupil only items from lessons she has COMPLETED, so each item is authored by the lesson that teaches it and added when that lesson is built. Lesson 1 has no Do-Now of its own; its five items are served from Lesson 2 onwards.

kp-platform-j2.label: How this website works
kp-platform-j2.note: Locks, saving, help, XP and the Workshop. Established J2 L1; every later lesson leans on it.

kp-rules-j2.label: The DT room rules
kp-rules-j2.note: Re-covered and tested in J2 L1's inspection rather than recited (his K4 ruling: assume nothing, measure instead).

kp-py-sequence.label: Python: steps run in order
kp-py-sequence.note: Established L2 in the block-to-Python bridge; the spine of L3-L5.

kp-py-variable.label: Python: storing a value in a variable
kp-py-variable.note: Carries J1's kp-variable forward into text code — one idea, two languages.

kp-py-input.label: Python: asking the user a question
kp-py-input.note: Established L3. Needs the runner's input() increment.

kp-py-selection.label: Python: choosing with if
kp-py-selection.note: Established L4. The direct descendant of J1's kp-ifelse.

kp-formula.label: Spreadsheet formulae and cell references
kp-formula.note: Established L6. New-engine flag on the grid: prototype before it is promised.

kp-chart-honesty.label: Reading a chart honestly
kp-chart-honesty.note: Established L7; the judgement half of the data block.

kp-malware.label: Malware and how it spreads
kp-malware.note: Established L10; opens the protect block.

kp-encryption.label: Encryption, and why HTTPS matters
kp-encryption.note: Established L11. Kid Krypto licence needed before the cipher-wheel kit prints.

kp-law.label: The UK laws about computers
kp-law.note: Established L12 by name: DPA/GDPR, Computer Misuse Act 1990, CDPA 1988.

kp-social-eng.label: Scams and how people are tricked

kp-html.label: HTML: the structure of a page

kp-css.label: CSS: how a page looks
kp-css.note: Established L15, used for real in L16.

items.stem: Órla scrolls down her year map on Monday and sees that Lesson 9 still has a padlock on its tile. What has to happen before she can open it?
options: Her teacher has to open Lesson 9 for the class
She has to finish Lessons 7 and 8 first
She has to wait until the date of that lesson comes round
She has to sign out and sign back in again

items.stem: Niamh answers a question in Lesson 3, then the bell goes and she signs out. Next fortnight her answer is still there. Why?
options: Because the website kept it the moment she typed it
Because she pressed the Save button before she left the room
Because the page was copied into her Google Drive
Because signing out puts your work away for you

items.stem: Saoirse's class gets to the DT room before the teacher. The door has been left unlocked and two pupils have already gone in and sat down. What should Saoirse do?
options: Wait in the line outside until the teacher comes
Go in and sit down, since the door is open anyway
Wait outside, but send somebody in to bring the two out
Run to the staffroom to fetch whichever teacher is free

items.stem: Sorcha sits down in the DT room and her mouse will not move the pointer. There is a spare mouse sitting on the shelf by the door. What should she do?
options: Put her hand up and tell the teacher straight away
Fetch the spare from the shelf and swap it in herself
Move to the free station at the end of the row
Get on with the lesson and mention it at the bell

items.stem: Aoife finishes Lesson 2 and clicks the Kit Locker at the top of her year map. What is waiting for her in there?
options: The new screen colours and badges she has unlocked
The answers she typed in Lesson 1 and Lesson 2
The lessons she has finished so far this year
A list of the equipment in the DT room

items.stem: Aoibhe's program starts with the line `print("Match day")`. What does that line do?
options: Puts the words Match day on the console
Makes a box called Match day and leaves it empty
Waits for somebody to type the words Match day
Checks whether the words Match day are already on the console

items.stem: Saoirse types `lives = 3` as the first line of her program. What has that line done?
options: Made a box called lives with 3 in it
Printed the number 3 on the console
Asked Python whether lives is the same as 3
Counted how many times the program has run

items.stem: Sorcha's line `print("Score: " + score)` stops with an error, and score holds the number 2. What does her line need?
options: str( ) around score, so the + has words on both sides
Speech marks around score, so Python can read it
The + changed to a comma, because numbers do not use +
Nothing — the error is on a different line

items.stem: Róisín's program reaches the line `town = input("Where do you live?")`. What happens on the screen next?
options: The question appears and the program waits until she types an answer
The question appears and the program carries straight on to the next line
The words Where do you live? are put into the box called town
Nothing appears until the whole program has finished running

items.stem: A pupil says the chatbot she built yesterday is clever, because it knew her name. What is the honest answer?
options: It was told her name by her, and it printed it back out
It looked her name up on the school system
It worked her name out from the way she typed
It remembered her name from the last time she used it

items.topic: Using an answer more than once
items.stem: Aoife's bot asks for a name once, and she wants it used in three different sentences. What does she need to do?
options: Nothing extra — she uses the same box name in all three lines
Ask the same question three times, once before each sentence
Make three boxes and copy the answer into each one
Put the answer in speech marks so it can be used again

items.stem: Ciara's program stops and the console says: NameError: name 'naem' is not defined. What has she most likely done?
options: Spelled a box name differently in two places
Forgotten to put speech marks round some words
Joined a number onto words without str( )
Left a space at the front of one of her lines

items.stem: A bot asks how old somebody is and they type 12. What is in the box afterwards?
options: The 1 and the 2, kept as writing
The number 12, ready to be added to
Nothing, because 12 is not words
Both — Python keeps it as writing and as a number

items.topic: Writing a question somebody can answer
items.stem: Which of these is the best question for a chatbot that a classmate has ten seconds to answer?
options: What is your favourite food?
What is the best thing that has ever happened to you?
What would you change about the school day, and why?
Describe your ideal weekend in one word
